note: Judgement: the nearest existing id for an African root. Brito calls batuque 'de origem africana'; Gonçalves (via pt Wikipedia) says it is not a transplanted continental genre but an adaptation of some African dance that developed its own character in Cape Verde. No source names a parent genre in the tree.

proposal: alias and marker of batuku, not a separate record
note: Finaçon is the improvised verse sung inside a batuku session, in the batuku rhythm, by the lead singer (en Wikipedia; Brito 1998). Recordings labelled finaçon (Ntóni Denti d'Oru, Nha Mita Pereira, Nácia Gomi) are batuku circle recordings. Represent it as an alias and the second marker, not a child genre. Caution: the 1980s-90s band Finaçon played funaná, so the alias must not pull that band's songs into batuku.

proposal: separate record later (sibling under n_capeverdeanmusic), not a child of batuku
note: Tabanka is a different Santiago (and Maio) tradition: a May-July procession and mutual-aid association with drums, conch shells and cornets in a fast binary rhythm, banned from the late 19th century. No source makes it a form of batuku; they share only island, colonial bans and the revival composers (Pantera wrote a 'Tabanca'). Give it its own record (id 'tabanka', proposed parent wadrum, judgement) in a later round; until then do not fold it into batuku.
